questions.question: Describe the role of plasmodesmata in plant development ?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Plasmodesmata play a crucial role in plant development by maintaining symplastic continuity
  • between cells, allowing the plant body to function as an integrated system. They facilitate the
  • movement of nutrients, metabolites, and growth regulators between adjacent cells, ensuring
  • coordinated growth and development. They also enable intercellular communication necessary for
  • cell differentiation and tissue formation, and maintain connectivity even in mature and thick-walled
  • cells. (Any 5 points)

questions.question: List out the functions of external secretory tissues
questions.solution_html:
• List out the functions of external secretory tissues
  • Ans: Functions of External Secretory Tissues
  • • Secrete substances (oils, mucilage, terpenes, resins, enzymes, etc.) for various plant
  • activities.
  • • Attract pollinators by secreting nectar (important for reproduction).
  • • Provide protection against herbivores by producing irritants, toxins, adhesives, and defensive
  • chemicals.
  • • Protect plants from pathogens through antimicrobial secretions and resin production.
  • • Help in wound healing by secretion of resins that seal damaged tissues.
  • • Aid in water retention and prevent desiccation (mucilage secretion).
  • • Regulate salt balance and excrete excess salts and water.
  • • Facilitate ecological interactions (e.g., attracting ants for plant defence via extrafloral
  • nectaries).
  • • Assist in trapping and digestion of insects in carnivorous plants (enzymes and adhesives).
questions.final_answer: • Assist in trapping and digestion of insects in carnivorous plants (enzymes and adhesives)

questions.question: Briefly explain the characteristics of compression wood.
questions.solution_html:
• Briefly explain the characteristics of compression wood.
  • Ans: Characteristics of Compression Wood
  • • Formed as reaction wood on the lower side of the stem due to increased cambial activity.
  • • Shows eccentric growth rings, making it easily identifiable.
  • • Heavier (15–40% more) than normal wood of the same species.
  • • Gradual transition from early wood to late wood (not distinct).
  • • Tracheids are round in cross-section with intercellular spaces.
  • • Cell walls thicker (especially spring wood) and higher lignin content.
  • • Wood is brittle with high and irregular longitudinal shrinkage.
  • • Lumber twists during drying due to uneven shrinkage.
questions.final_answer: • Lumber twists during drying due to uneven shrinkage

questions.question: With suitable examples, explain how anatomical characters used for / identification of adulterance on crude drugs.
questions.solution_html:
• With suitable examples, explain how anatomical characters used for identification of
  • adulterance on crude drugs. / (Give full marks for answers that include four
  • relevant points along with one example).
  • Ans: Anatomical characters are essential for identifying adulterants in crude drugs, especially when
  • they are in dried, broken, or powdered forms where external features are lost. Since internal structures
  • remain stable, microscopic examination provides reliable identification.
  • Each plant species has unique anatomical features such as epidermal cells, stomata, trichomes, fibres
  • vessels, crystals, and starch grains. These act as diagnostic markers to distinguish genuine drugs from
  • adulterants. Powder microscopy is widely used, as it allows quick analysis of small samples.
  • Epidermal characters like cell shape and stomatal types (anomocytic, anisocytic, etc.) help detect
  • adulteration. Trichomes are highly specific and resistant, making them reliable indicators. For
  • example, absence of characteristic trichomes suggests substitution.
  • Supporting tissues such as fibres and sclereids (stone cells) also aid identification. Similarly, xylem
  • vessels show distinct thickening patterns like spiral or pitted, which remain visible after grinding.
  • Calcium oxalate crystals (raphides, druses, prisms) are species-specific and useful markers. Starch
  • grains and secretory structures like oil cells and ducts further support identification. Microchemical
  • tests (iodine for starch, phloroglucinol for lignin) confirm these features.
  • Examples:True cinnamon (Cinnamomum verum) is distinguished from cassia (Cinnamomum cassia)
  • by fibre structure, and senna (Senna alexandrina) by its characteristic leaf constants. Haitian bark
  • can be distinguished from Bolivian Guarea bark by their differences in phloem fibre arrangement.
questions.final_answer: can be distinguished from Bolivian Guarea bark by their differences in phloem fibre arrangement

questions.question: How wood is modified for industrial use through physical methods? What are / its advantage?
questions.solution_html:
• advantage?
  • Ans: Physical modification primarily involves heat treatment, commonly referred to as thermal
  • modification. In this process, wood is exposed to elevated temperatures, generally between 160°C
  • and 260°C, under controlled conditions with limited or no oxygen to prevent combustion. During
  • thermal treatment, hemicelluloses undergo degradation, and the number of free hydroxyl groups
  • decreases. This reduces the wood’s ability to absorb moisture. Chemical changes in lignin also occur
  • leading to improved dimensional stability and resistance to fungal attack. The process will improve
  • qualities like reduced equilibrium moisture content, resistance to fungal decay, enhanced color
  • uniformity (wood becomes darker and aesthetically appealing) and Reduced hygroscopicity.
  • Thermally modified wood is widely used in exterior cladding, decking, window frames, and other
  • applications where dimensional stability is important.
questions.final_answer: applications where dimensional stability is important

questions.question: Differentiate between albuminous seeds and exalbuminous seeds?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Seeds are classified as albuminous or exalbuminous based on the presence or absence of
  • endosperm in the mature seed.
  • Albuminous seeds
  • ● Endosperm present in mature seed
  • ● Food stored in endosperm
  • ● Embryo small
  • ● Examples: maize, wheat, castor
  • Exalbuminous seeds
  • ● Endosperm absent in mature seed
  • ● Food stored in cotyledons
  • ● Embryo large
questions.final_answer: ● Embryo large

questions.question: Explain the structure of a typical female gametophyte.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The female gametophyte generally contains 7 cells with a total of 8 nuclei: one egg cell, two
  • synergid cells, three antipodal cells, and a central cell with two polar nuclei.
  • • Egg cell: The single cell that fuses with a sperm cell to form the zygote.
  • • Synergids (2 cells): Located near the micropyle, they help guide the pollen tube for
  • fertilization.
  • • Antipodal cells (3 cells): Found at the chalazal end, thought to nourish the embryo sac though
  • their function varies.
  • • Central cell: Contains two polar nuclei which fuse with a sperm nucleus to form the triploid
  • endosperm, supporting the developing embryo.
  • (Description: (3 marks), Diagram (2 Marks))
  • Essay
questions.final_answer: Essay

questions.question: Explain seasonal activity of cambium and formation of annual rings. Add a / note on dendrochronology.
questions.solution_html:
• dendrochronology.
  • Ans: The vascular cambium is a lateral meristem responsible for secondary growth in woody plants
  • and its activity varies with seasonal changes in environmental conditions. During favourable seasons
  • such as spring or the rainy period, the cambium becomes highly active and produces a large amount
  • of secondary xylem and secondary phloem. The xylem elements formed during this period are large
  • in size, thin-walled, and have a wide lumen; this type of wood is known as early wood (spring
  • wood). Early wood is generally lighter in colour and less dense. In contrast, during unfavourable
  • seasons such as winter or dry summer, the activity of the cambium slows down or becomes almost
  • dormant. As a result, the xylem elements formed are smaller, thick-walled, and have a narrow lumen;
  • this is called late wood (autumn wood), which is darker and denser.
  • The alternate formation of early wood and late wood during successive seasons leads to the
  • development of distinct concentric rings in the stem, known as annual rings. Each annual ring consists
  • of one band of early wood followed by a band of late wood, representing one year of growth. These
  • rings are clearly visible in the transverse section of the stem due to the difference in structure and
  • density between early and late wood. The number of annual rings helps in determining the age of the
  • plant, and their thickness reflects the growth conditions during each year.
  • Dendrochronology
  • Dendrochronology is the scientific method of studying annual rings to determine the age of trees and
  • to analyse past climatic and environmental conditions. By counting the number of annual rings, the
  • exact age of a tree can be estimated. Moreover, the width of the rings provides information about the
  • environmental conditions prevailing during each year. Wider rings indicate favourable conditions
  • such as sufficient rainfall, optimal temperature, and adequate nutrients, while narrower rings suggest
  • unfavourable conditions like drought or environmental stress. Dendrochronology is widely used in
  • fields such as climatology, ecology, and archaeology, where it helps in reconstructing past climates
  • and dating ancient wooden artifacts.
questions.final_answer: and dating ancient wooden artifacts
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the process and significance of syngamy and triple fusion
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: In angiosperms, fertilization involves two fusion events—syngamy and triple fusion
  • collectively known as double fertilization.
  • Process of Syngamy
  • ● One male gamete (sperm) fuses with the egg cell inside the embryo sac
  • ● Results in the formation of a diploid (2n) zygote
  • ● This process occurs at the micropylar end of the embryo sac
  • Significance of Syngamy
  • ● Leads to formation of zygote, which develops into the embryo
  • ● Maintains diploid chromosome number
  • Process of Triple Fusion
  • ● The second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei in the central cell
  • ● Forms a triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus (PEN)
  • ● This process is called triple fusion
  • ● Occurs in the central cell of the embryo sac
  • Significance of Triple Fusion
  • ● Develops into endosperm, which provides nourishment to the embryo
  • ● Ensures synchronization of embryo and endosperm development
  • ● Prevents wastage of resources (endosperm forms only after fertilization)
questions.final_answer: ● Prevents wastage of resources (endosperm forms only after fertilization)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

  • Thermally modified wood is widely used in exterior cladding, decking, window frames, and other
  • applications where dimensional stability is important.

questions.question: Differentiate between albuminous seeds and exalbuminous seeds?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Seeds are classified as albuminous or exalbuminous based on the presence or absence of
  • endosperm in the mature seed.
  • Albuminous seeds
  • ● Endosperm present in mature seed
  • ● Food stored in endosperm
  • ● Embryo small
  • ● Examples: maize, wheat, castor
  • Exalbuminous seeds
  • ● Endosperm absent in mature seed
  • ● Food stored in cotyledons
  • ● Embryo large
questions.final_answer: ● Embryo large

questions.question: Explain the structure of a typical female gametophyte.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The female gametophyte generally contains 7 cells with a total of 8 nuclei: one egg cell, two
  • synergid cells, three antipodal cells, and a central cell with two polar nuclei.
  • • Egg cell: The single cell that fuses with a sperm cell to form the zygote.
  • • Synergids (2 cells): Located near the micropyle, they help guide the pollen tube for
  • fertilization.
  • • Antipodal cells (3 cells): Found at the chalazal end, thought to nourish the embryo sac though
  • their function varies.
  • • Central cell: Contains two polar nuclei which fuse with a sperm nucleus to form the triploid
  • endosperm, supporting the developing embryo.

questions.question: Explain seasonal activity of cambium and formation of annual rings. Add a / note on dendrochronology.
questions.solution_html:
• dendrochronology.
  • Ans: The vascular cambium is a lateral meristem responsible for secondary growth in woody plants
  • and its activity varies with seasonal changes in environmental conditions. During favourable seasons
  • such as spring or the rainy period, the cambium becomes highly active and produces a large amount
  • of secondary xylem and secondary phloem. The xylem elements formed during this period are large
  • in size, thin-walled, and have a wide lumen; this type of wood is known as early wood (spring
  • wood). Early wood is generally lighter in colour and less dense. In contrast, during unfavourable
  • seasons such as winter or dry summer, the activity of the cambium slows down or becomes almost
  • dormant. As a result, the xylem elements formed are smaller, thick-walled, and have a narrow lumen;
  • this is called late wood (autumn wood), which is darker and denser.
  • The alternate formation of early wood and late wood during successive seasons leads to the
  • development of distinct concentric rings in the stem, known as annual rings. Each annual ring consists
  • of one band of early wood followed by a band of late wood, representing one year of growth. These
  • rings are clearly visible in the transverse section of the stem due to the difference in structure and
  • density between early and late wood. The number of annual rings helps in determining the age of the
  • plant, and their thickness reflects the growth conditions during each year.
  • Dendrochronology
  • Dendrochronology is the scientific method of studying annual rings to determine the age of trees and
  • to analyse past climatic and environmental conditions. By counting the number of annual rings, the
  • exact age of a tree can be estimated. Moreover, the width of the rings provides information about the
  • environmental conditions prevailing during each year. Wider rings indicate favourable conditions
  • such as sufficient rainfall, optimal temperature, and adequate nutrients, while narrower rings suggest
  • unfavourable conditions like drought or environmental stress. Dendrochronology is widely used in
  • fields such as climatology, ecology, and archaeology, where it helps in reconstructing past climates
  • and dating ancient wooden artifacts.
questions.final_answer: and dating ancient wooden artifacts

questions.question: Discuss the process and significance of syngamy and triple fusion
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: In angiosperms, fertilization involves two fusion events—syngamy and triple fusion
  • collectively known as double fertilization.
  • Process of Syngamy
  • ● One male gamete (sperm) fuses with the egg cell inside the embryo sac
  • ● Results in the formation of a diploid (2n) zygote
  • ● This process occurs at the micropylar end of the embryo sac
  • Significance of Syngamy
  • ● Leads to formation of zygote, which develops into the embryo
  • ● Maintains diploid chromosome number
  • Process of Triple Fusion
  • ● The second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei in the central cell
  • ● Forms a triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus (PEN)
  • ● This process is called triple fusion
  • ● Occurs in the central cell of the embryo sac
  • Significance of Triple Fusion
  • ● Develops into endosperm, which provides nourishment to the embryo
  • ● Ensures synchronization of embryo and endosperm development
  • ● Prevents wastage of resources (endosperm forms only after fertilization)
questions.final_answer: ● Prevents wastage of resources (endosperm forms only after fertilization)
